cards.explanation: The answer is the ways of the kings of Israel. Jehoram, king of Judah, walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. Ahab was Israel's king (1 Kings 16:29), and Jehoram married one of his daughters. The text puts those two things side by side, and I'll let everybody do the math.
The answer is True. Verse 18 says Jehoram "…did evil in the sight of the LORD." The text comes right out and says it. I think that's a heavy thing to read about a king.

The answer is False. Verse 19 says the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah. The reason is His servant David, and He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. Judah is still standing, friends, and the promise is the reason why.

The answer is that He promised to keep a lamp for David forever. Verse 19 says He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. David was Israel's king long before this (2 Samuel 5:3). So the reason is a promise, and the text names it plainly.

The answer is king. Verse 20 says Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and "…appointed their own king." They set up their own leader, like a crew that quits and opens its own shop across the street.

The answer is that he rises up and attacks by night. When the Edomites surrounded Jehoram and his chariot commanders at Zair, he "…rose up and attacked by night." The text gives the action and leaves out the plan, so I'll leave it out too.
The answer is False. Verse 21 says his troops "…fled to their homes." The word "however" shows the turn right there, friends. The king attacked, and his men were headed down the road.

The answer is that Edom is still rebelling when this was written. Verse 22 says "…to this day Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah." The writer is telling us it was still going when this was written. Libnah rebelled at the same time too.

The answer is the City of David. Verse 24 says Jehoram "…was buried with them in the City of David." His son Ahaziah then reigned in his place. One king laid to rest, and the next one is already on the way to the throne.
The answer is Omri king of Israel. Verse 26 says Athaliah was the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel. That's a big clue for the next verse, bakers. Ahaziah's mother came from Israel's royal family.

The answer is False. Verse 27 says Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD. It also says he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab. The text gives no turnaround.

The answer is Joram son of Ahab. Verse 28 says Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. Joram is the king of Israel. Judah's king and Israel's king are headed to the same battle.
The answer is True. Verse 28 says "…the Arameans wounded Joram." Joram is king of Israel and the son of Ahab. In the next verse he returns to Jezreel to recover.

The answer is visit. Verse 29 says Ahaziah went down to Jezreel "…to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded." Think of dropping by with a plate of cookies when somebody's laid up, friends.
